packages/agent.rationale: Durable harness lifecycle and recovery seams are authoritative for server-owned operations.

packages/ai.rationale: Provider and model APIs remain independent of the fork daemon boundary.

packages/client.rationale: The v2 client owns protocol validation, reconnect cursors, and transport lifecycle at the fork boundary.

packages/codex-plugin-compat.rationale: Codex manifest and resource adaptation uses provider-neutral registries without changing Pi provider APIs.

packages/coding-agent.rationale: The configured daemon and server-owned coding-agent service define fork lifecycle, ownership, and compatibility behavior.

packages/diagnostics.rationale: Diagnostic contracts are reusable, while durable persistence and bundle ownership are supplied by the fork server.

packages/evals.rationale: Evaluation helpers do not depend on the daemon or fork protocol.

packages/file-references.rationale: Reference parsing is reusable, but remote resolution and upload semantics require the fork server boundary.

packages/model-instructions.rationale: Profile matching is reusable, while resolved-model freezing is supplied by the server runtime host.

packages/protocol.rationale: Versioned v2 schemas, cursors, and error envelopes are authoritative fork protocol contracts.

packages/server-extension-api.rationale: The public extension contract is reusable but requires the fork server runtime to execute durably.

packages/server.rationale: Transport, leases, authorization, persistence projections, and recovery are server-owned invariants.

packages/session-backends/sqlite-node.rationale: SQLite transactions and derived-state repair implement the authoritative durable session boundary.

packages/session-naming.rationale: Naming policy consumes public model and session seams and has no protocol ownership.

packages/telemetry.rationale: Telemetry contracts are runtime-neutral and carry no fork-specific authority.

packages/tui.rationale: TUI components remain reusable; remote views consume snapshots through the client adapter.

packages/web-tools.rationale: Provider-neutral web operations are reusable, but safety, bounds, and provenance are enforced by the fork server.
